 That was a cracking contest between two evenly matched teams. There were two superb hundreds from either side, but Hamza Zahoor's knock eclipsed Arjun Rathod's. But this tournament is all about recognising future stars, and India and Pakistan might have unearthed a couple of them. That's all from this game. Until next time, goodbye and stay safe.. Hamza Zahoor | Player of the Match: Since I had to go all the way, my mindset was that I would stay till the end and win it. I will go till the last. [Did you feel the pressure when those wickets fell towards the end?] No, there wasn't that much pressure. I was enjoying myself, playing my game and enjoying the game. Farhan Yousaf: Second win in this tournament, and I'm very proud of my guys. Early on, we collapsed, a couple of wickets, but that was an amazing innings from Hamza and Hasnain Dar. [On his bowlers' performance and restricting India to 208] Yes, I already told you before the match, on this pitch, difficult to decide whether we go with the ball first or we go with the bat first. So, we utilised the opportunity early on. Little bit moisture on the pitch, and we utilised the opportunity as well. [On Hamza Zahoor] Yes, exactly. But I'm not surprised about Hamza. I know the ability of the guy. I am not surprised by Hamza's innings today. But I really appreciate the way he assessed the condition and played according to the situation. [On sealing their spot for the semifinal] Yes, we're looking for the next match, not the semi-final. We go with full intent in the next match, and then we decide. Lakshya Raichandani: Yeah, they weren't enough. We were 20-30 runs short, but overall there were some good innings from Arjun and a 20 good contribution from KP (Kavya Patel). Yeah, it was a really good innings, and if one would have stayed there with him (Arjun), it could have been a little bit more total. Yeah, definitely. We will try to rectify, and there was a lot of positive from this game. And we will try to take that forward. Yeah, there were some really good efforts, they were 60 for 5. We could have bowled a little bit better. But overall, it was really good. 16:45 Local Time, 12:45 GMT, 18:15 IST: What a game! It ebbed and flowed from one side to the other, in the end, Hamza Zahoor and Pakistan held their nerve to claim victory. Chasing 209, they kept losing wickets at regular intervals and were reduced to 61 for 5. Zahoor walked in at that stage and took the game on, Hasnain Dar played the supporting role at the other end. The duo stitched a 107-run stand for the sixth wicket, putting Pakistan ahead. Just when it seemed they would get Pakistan over the line, a couple of wickets fell including Dar's, leaving Zahoor to take the responsibility. He did that magnificently, farming the strike towards the end and sealing the contest with an unbeaten 100. Early on, Arjun Rathod bailed India out of trouble with a superb hundred, helping them reach 208, which was not enough. Hang around for the presentations.. 48.1 H Kavya Patel to Hamza Zahoor, FOUR , Pakistan win by 3 wickets. Look at Hamza Zahoor go. He's pumped. As soon as the ball went past the fielder, he was off running towards the Pakistan supporters. He's taken his helmet off and roaring in the delight along with fist pumps. Shafiq runs across to catch up with him and so do the rest of his team mates. He removes a note from his pocket and shows it towards the crowd. What a knock! He came in with the team struggling, counterattacked and added a 100+ stand with Dar, when a couple of wickets fell, he subdued himself and took Pakistan over the line. "Tomorrow match 50 Hamza Zahoor" - is what the note reads . He's doubled that. Terrific hundred. Coming to the ball: Low full toss outside off, Zahoor presses across and drives in front of square, once the ball beat the diving extra cover fielder, Zahoor was off on a celebratory run Kavya Patel [9.0-0-44-1] is back into the attack Over 48 205-7 1 Wd Wd 0 0 0 0 0 ( 3 runs) Niqab Shafiq 2 (16) Hamza Zahoor 96 (107) Ishan Sood 9-2-36-1 Over Summary View all overs 47.6 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, no run, angling into leg, Shafiq turns it gently towards mid-wicket 47.5 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, no run, yorker on leg, Shafiq watchfully digs it out to mid-on 47.4 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, no run, back of a length delivery, Shafiq rides the bounce and angles it to backward point 47.3 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, no run, good length ball on off, Shafiq defends with soft hands to the off-side 47.2 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, no run, fullish delivery on leg, Shafiq blocks with a straight bat 47.2 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, wide , this is poor. Sood is clearly uncomfortable bowling from round the wicket. The last one was close to the guideline, but this was well away. Easy call for the umpire. Just 4 needed.. 47.2 Ishan Sood to Niqab Shafiq, wide , sprays it outside off, Shafiq leaves and picks up the wide. Zahoor claps from the other end Once again Zahoor walks across, has a quick chat and punch of the gloves with Shafiq. Five balls in the over. What will Shafiq do? Sood has gone round the wicket 47.1 Ishan Sood to Hamza Zahoor, 1 run, full and outside off, Zahoor pats it to cover-point and quickly crosses over Over 47 202-7 1 0 0 1 1 0 ( 3 runs) Niqab Shafiq 2 (11) Hamza Zahoor 95 (106) Mohit Ulva 10-0-45-2 Over Summary View all overs 46.6 Mohit Ulva to Niqab Shafiq, no run, good length ball close to off, Shafiq defends to backward point 46.5 Mohit Ulva to Hamza Zahoor, 1 run, good length ball outside off, Zahoor guides it past backward point and settles with a single 46.4 Mohit Ulva to Niqab Shafiq, 1 run, on a length and outside off, Shafiq angles it down to third man Zahoor walks across and has a word.
